title: Identifying Conics from Equations
short: Complete the square to name and graph any conic.

blocks.html: Circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas all have equations of the form $Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0$ once you multiply everything out. Given such an equation, you can name the conic at a glance, then complete the square to find its center or vertex and match a standard form from parabolas, ellipses or hyperbolas.

For $Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0$ (a genuine conic, not a degenerate one): $A = C$: circle; $A$ and $C$ the same sign: ellipse; opposite signs: hyperbola; only one squared term: parabola. If there is an $xy$ term, use $B^2 - 4AC$: negative for an ellipse, zero for a parabola, positive for a hyperbola.

Completing the square only shifts the curve; it never changes the coefficients of $x^2$ and $y^2$. So those coefficients already tell you which standard form you will reach: two squares added (ellipse or circle), two squares subtracted (hyperbola), or one square (parabola). The $xy$ term rotates the curve, and $B^2 - 4AC$ is the combination that rotation does not change.

blocks.title: An ellipse
steps: $A = 4$ and $C = 9$ have the same sign and are different: an ellipse.
Complete the squares, adding $4 \cdot 4 = 16$ and $9 \cdot 1 = 9$ to both sides: $4(x - 2)^2 + 9(y + 1)^2 = 36$.

blocks.title: A hyperbola
blocks.q: Identify $x^2 - y^2 + 4x + 2y - 1 = 0$ and find its center.
blocks.a: Hyperbola with center $(-2, 1)$, opening left and right

blocks.html: Completing the square inside a factored group but adding the wrong amount to the other side. In $4(x^2 - 4x + 4)$ the $+4$ inside the parentheses is really $+16$, because it is multiplied by $4$. Add $16$ to the other side, not $4$.
